product_metadata.description: Bitcoin is the original cryptocurrency and the largest digital asset by market value. It is widely viewed as a decentralized store of value and the benchmark for the broader crypto market. Many traders use BTC as the reference asset for crypto sentiment, liquidity, and risk appetite. Its fixed supply and long operating history are central to its appeal. Major macro, ETF, regulatory, and institutional developments often show up in Bitcoin first.
product_metadata.index_provider: CF Benchmarks' Bitcoin Real Time Index

product_metadata.description: Ether is the native asset of Ethereum, the largest smart-contract blockchain in crypto. Ethereum powers a broad ecosystem that includes decentralized finance, stablecoins, NFTs, token issuance, and many onchain applications. ETH is used to pay transaction fees and secure the network through staking. It is often treated as the main benchmark for crypto application activity and smart-contract adoption. Network upgrades, fee trends, ETF developments, and staking flows can all influence how traders price ETH.
product_metadata.index_provider: CF Benchmarks' Ether-Dollar Real Time Index

product_metadata.description:
Gold is a physical metal that has functioned as a store of value for thousands of years and is widely used as a hedge against inflation and currency weakness.

Key factors in play: Central banks have been buying gold at an elevated pace in recent years, according to the World Gold Council, as some countries look to reduce their reliance on the US dollar. Periods of geopolitical tension also tend to boost demand for gold as a safer place to hold money. Because gold pays no interest, its price is also sensitive to Federal Reserve policy, rate expectations, and overall US dollar strength.

What to watch: Federal Reserve meetings, CPI/PPI inflation releases, and comments from Fed officials.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Gold Reference Rate

product_metadata.description: Solana is a high-speed blockchain built for low-cost transactions and large-scale consumer activity. SOL is used for transaction fees, staking, and participating in the Solana ecosystem. Traders often associate Solana with strong retail momentum and fast-moving onchain activity. Its market narrative is closely tied to adoption, network reliability, and the pace of new app launches.

product_metadata.description: XRP is the native asset of the XRP Ledger, a blockchain designed for fast and low-cost value transfers. XRP has been a major asset in the market for years and often trades on both adoption narratives and regulatory headlines. Its price can react sharply to developments involving Ripple, exchange access, and policy clarity in the United States. Many traders view it as a payments-focused large-cap crypto with a distinct legal and institutional story.
product_metadata.index_provider: CF Benchmarks' XRP-Dollar Real Time Index

product_metadata.description:
Silver combines two roles: it's held for some of the same reasons as gold, as protection against inflation or a weak dollar, and it's also an industrial material used in solar panels, electronics, and EVs.

Key factors in play: The world has used more silver than it's mined for several years running, according to the Silver Institute, driven mainly by growing demand from solar panels and other manufacturing. The U.S. added silver to its list of critical minerals in 2025, reflecting its industrial importance. Solar makers have also been working to use less silver per panel to cut costs, which could ease that shortage over time. Silver's price still tends to move with the same broader forces as gold, like the Fed, the dollar, and inflation data.

What to watch: How silver trades relative to gold (the "gold/silver ratio"), Federal Reserve meetings, and CPI releases.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Silver Reference Rate

product_metadata.description:
Kalshi offers exposure to large U.S. technology and growth companies through Kalshi's US Tech 100 index perpetual future. The underlying index is calculated by MerQube (https://merqube.com/indices/MQBUSTQT), which has historically shown 99%+ daily-return correlation with major U.S. technology benchmarks, including the Nasdaq-100®. It's a total return index, which means dividends are reinvested back into the index.

The index is made up of 100 large non-financial companies, many of them in technology. It is weighted by market capitalization, so the biggest companies like Nvidia, Meta and Google move the price much more than smaller ones. Because the index is concentrated in fewer companies and sectors than a broad 500-company index, it can move more sharply in either direction.

What to watch: Earnings from the largest tech companies, spending on AI and data centers, Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions, and monthly inflation reports.
product_metadata.index_provider: MerQube US Tech 100 TR Index

product_metadata.description:
WTI (West Texas Intermediate) is the main U.S. crude oil benchmark. This contract is a long-dated future with a 10-year expiration. Prices are driven mostly by global supply and demand. Supply depends on how much major oil-exporting countries and U.S. producers put out, and can be disrupted by conflicts or sanctions. Demand tends to follow the health of the global economy and seasonal patterns, such as summer travel. U.S. crude inventories show whether the market has more oil than it needs or not enough.

What to watch: Production decisions by major oil-exporting countries, weekly U.S. crude inventory reports, conflicts in oil-producing regions, and global economic data.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth

product_metadata.description:
Palladium is a precious metal used almost entirely for one purpose: catalytic converters in gasoline vehicles.

Key factors in play: Palladium's price has declined as its main use case shrinks. Automakers have been shifting to EVs, which don't need catalytic converters, and substituting cheaper platinum where they can. That's pushed demand down over time, and some forecasters, including the WPIC and Heraeus, expect a market surplus. On the supply side, a large share of palladium comes from Russia and South Africa, so sanctions or mining disruptions in either country can affect the price.

What to watch: Tariff and sanctions news, auto sales data, and Federal Reserve meetings.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Palladium Reference Rate

product_metadata.description:
Platinum is a precious metal used in diesel catalytic converters (which reduce vehicle emissions), fuel cells, and jewelry.

Key factors in play: Platinum's price mostly comes down to a tug of war between constrained supply and shifting demand. Mining disruptions in South Africa, the largest producer, have kept output tight, according to the World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC). Jewelry buying and hybrid vehicle catalyst use have been demand drivers, while rising EV adoption works in the other direction, since EVs need no catalytic converter at all.

What to watch: Gold price moves, Federal Reserve meetings, CPI releases, and South African mine supply news.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Platinum Reference Rate

product_metadata.description:
Uniswap is a popular app for trading crypto directly with other people, no bank or exchange needed. UNI is its token. For a long time, owning UNI mainly just gave you a vote in how Uniswap is run.

Key factors in play: Uniswap now takes a small cut of trading fees and uses it to permanently remove some UNI from circulation. This means the more people use Uniswap, the more it can affect UNI's supply. Changes in how governments regulate trading platforms like this can also affect how much people use Uniswap, and in turn, UNI's price.

What to watch: How much people are trading on Uniswap, votes on fee changes, and overall activity in the crypto market.
product_metadata.index_provider: CF Benchmarks' Uniswap-Dollar Real Time Index

product_metadata.description:
Copper is a reddish metal used to carry electricity and heat, found in wiring, pipes, electronics, and EVs. Its price tracks global building and manufacturing activity. In recent years, global copper usage has outpaced new mine supply, partly because new mines take a long time to develop, though recycling and new production projects are also part of the supply picture. Demand has grown from EVs, power grids, and the wiring needed for AI data centers, while trade policies and tariffs can affect how easily copper moves around the world.

What to watch: Global manufacturing and construction data, AI and data center buildout news, and trade policy between major economies.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Copper Reference Rate

product_metadata.description:
Aluminum is a lightweight metal used in cars, airplanes, packaging, and construction. It's generally cheaper and lighter than copper, which makes it common for industries needing materials in large volumes. Its price has been affected by tariffs on US imports, sanctions on some major producers, and energy costs, since making aluminum from raw ore requires a lot of electricity. Construction activity, car manufacturing, and global trade conditions also affect demand.

What to watch: Tariff and trade policy news, energy prices in major producing regions, and global manufacturing and construction data.
product_metadata.index_provider: Pyth Aluminum Reference Rate
